title:
—He had a sudden death, poor fellow, he said.
 
 —The best death, Mr Bloom said.
 
 Their wide open eyes looked at him.
 
 —No suffering, he said. A moment and all is over. Like dying in sleep.
 
 No-one spoke.
html_source: Bloom’s practical appraisal of Paddy Dignam’s death subtly indicates his irreligiosity: since he ignores the fact that, for a Catholic believer, sudden death without confession is frightful. Dying in a state of mortal sin could result in eternal damnation.
